banner: Decision support only. Your dispatch protocol governs.
title: Dispatch board
intro: For 911 call takers. See if a known fire explains the smoke where the caller is.
replay.strip: Replay · Aug 25, 2025. Recorded data, not today’s.
stored: Nothing about a call is stored or sent: the place, the answers and the drafts stay on this screen, and are gone when it closes.
public: Not a call taker? If you see flames or a smoke column, call 911.
place.label: Caller’s town or city
place.hint: Type a few letters, then press Enter.
place.none: No place matches. Check the spelling.
place.none.replay: No place matches. The replay has these towns: {towns}.
listen.off: Listen is off: this browser has no English voice that works on the device, and the board sends nothing to a voice service.
answer.title: Answer
answer.empty: Type the caller’s town to see the answer here.
answer.error.title: Not checked
answer.error: The fire and wind data did not load, so the board cannot say where this smoke is from. That does not mean there is no fire.
answer.close: This fire is close to the caller’s town: {km}.
facts.title: The facts and their sources
burn.ban.body: A burn ban is in effect {inProvince}.
burn.ban.source: From the province’s news release of {date} ({who}).
burn.notChecked.body: The board has no burn status for this place and day. That does not mean burning is allowed.
notes.copied: Copied. Paste it into your call notes.
notes.failed: The browser did not allow the copy. The notes are selected below: press Ctrl+C.
notes.label: Call notes
notes.head: Smoke check
notes.replay: Replay of Aug 25, 2025: recorded data, not today’s.
script.title: Ask the caller
script.about: The public app’s three questions, with the same routing: any yes or not sure goes to dispatch.
script.q2: What does the sky look like: smoke rising from one spot, grey haze everywhere, or only a smell?
script.keys: Keyboard: once on the answers, press an answer’s number.
outcome.title: Result:
outcome.dispatch.text: A yes or a not sure: there may be a fire near the caller.
outcome.dispatch.ban: A fire pit or bonfire, and a burn ban is in effect {inProvince}.
outcome.dispatch.noBurn: A fire pit or bonfire, and the province allows no burning there today ({where}).
outcome.pit.text: Dispatch if it is out of control, or if burning is banned. Burn status: {status}.
outcome.noFire.drifting: This fits the known smoke from {fire}, {km} away.
outcome.noFire.unclear: The trace is unclear: it may be smoke from {fire}, or something close by.
outcome.noFire.unexplained: No known fire explains this smoke. A new fire can take hours to show up in satellite data.
outcome.noFire.noPlace: Type the caller’s town to see if a known fire explains the smoke.
outcome.noFire.notChecked: The smoke’s source could not be checked. That does not mean there is no fire.
surge.title: Known smoke event
surge.intro: Many calls about the same smoke? Mark it as a known smoke event, and the board drafts a public message for your fire department’s social media.
surge.mark: Mark as a known smoke event
surge.no.answer: A draft needs an answer first: type the caller’s town.
surge.no.notDrifting: No draft for {town}: the trace does not link the smoke there to a known fire.
surge.no.close: No draft for {town}: the fire is close ({km}). People there need official instructions, not a message about distant smoke.
surge.never: Nothing is posted for you. Read each message, change what you need, then copy the text and download the image to post them yourself.
surge.failed: The browser did not allow the copy. Select the text and press Ctrl+C.
surge.alt.lead: Image description, for the post’s alt text:
surge.alt: {line}. A map shows the smoke’s path from {fire} to {town}. {call}
msg.smoke: The smoke in {town} today comes from {fire} {inProvince}, {km} km away.
msg.smoke.noProvince: The smoke in {town} today comes from {fire}, {km} km away.
msg.call: If you see flames or smoke from a building or vehicle, call 911.
img.sources: Sources: NASA FIRMS, Natural Resources Canada, GFS winds (Open-Meteo). Made with Smoke or Fire?
voice.intro: This is the dispatch board. Type the caller’s town to see if a known fire explains the smoke there. Then ask the caller the three questions.
voice.drifting: {town}. Drifting smoke, most likely from {fire}, about {distance} away, to the {direction}.
voice.drifting.under: {town}. Drifting smoke, most likely from {fire}, less than one kilometre away.
voice.unclear: {town}. It’s unclear. It may be smoke from {fire}, or something close by.
voice.unexplained: {town}. Unexplained smoke. No known fire explains it.
